reason: The hidden run prints 18 dots and then aborts, i.e. PHPUnit died exactly in test_restore_course (the 19th test and the first one that restores from a template course), before the two new tests were even reached; BEFORE/AFTER runs complete all 44 tests. So the agent's add_restore_course_summary_step()/tool_uploadcourse\local\restore_course_summary_step path (a custom restore_structure_step appended to restore_course_task after the plan is built) triggers a fatal during restore_controller::execute_plan(), which is a defect independent of the test API (the hidden tests only call tool_uploadcourse_course::prepare/proceed and inspect course.summary and the overviewfiles area, no human-only names). Statically the step's code looks plausible and I could not pinpoint the exact fatal, hence moderate confidence; the human instead threads $skiptemplatefields through restore_controller into restore_course_structure_step.

Agent result is identical to the BEFORE run (Errors: 2) because both hidden tests require_once fixtures under lib/tests/fixtures/core_renderer/ (before_help_icon_rendered_*_callbacks.php / _hooks.php) that the developers added and that are not copied over the agent patch. The agent's hook has the same FQCN \core\hook\output\before_help_icon_rendered and the exact methods the fixtures call (add_before_icon(string), add_after_icon(string), set_replacement(string)), and render_help_icon() emits before+template+after or the replacement, so the assertions (custom-replacement present, no data-bs-toggle="popover", before/after ordering) would pass if the fixtures existed. Only the constructor signature differs (renderer, identifier, component, context vs helpicon, renderer, templatecontext), which the tests never call directly.

The fast path and the request cache in get_course_progress_percentage() match the issue, and the agent keyed/purged the cache in internal_set_data() exactly as the issue proposes; the perf test assertions (fewer reads, 0 reads on repeat call, 50%) are satisfiable by the agent's code. However the agent purges only in internal_set_data(), not in delete_course_completion_data()/delete_all_state() (and delete_all_completion_data via them), so within one request the cache returns a stale 100% after criteria unlock, course reset or activity deletion; hidden tests test_course_progress_cache_invalidated_by_* assertEquals(0, ...) catch this and the agent run shows a failure. Serving a stale percentage after a reset in the same request is a real cache-invalidation defect a maintainer would reject, although the issue text only listed internal_set_data as purge point, so this is borderline with A. Cache name differs too (core_completion/progress_percentage vs core/course_progress) but the tests' purge() calls on the human name do not cause the failure.

The agent's change to utils::data_exportdata() is functionally identical to the human's ((string) cast, $contents !== '' instead of !empty, no final !empty() reset), so the new hidden test test_export_csv_values_match_export_text_value (assertSame('0', $datarow[0]/[1]) and the HTML textarea value) would pass. The failure (14 assertions, 1 failure, fewer than BEFORE) comes from the pre-existing test_export_csv: the agent also edited the fixture CSVs test_data_export_with_files.csv / test_data_export_without_files.csv to add zerotextfield/zeronumberfield columns to match its own extended get_data(), but the hidden test file restored the original 5-field get_data() while the agent's modified fixtures stayed on disk, so the exported CSV no longer equals the fixture. This is a fixture/test-infrastructure mismatch, not a behaviour defect.

The issue says get_import_map() should emit a modulepreload link 'for each concrete, active-theme import map entry' and lists react, react-dom, tabbable, bootstrap and the design-system bundle; the agent implemented exactly that shape-based filter (get_preload_urls(): skip prefix entries and per-theme variants) and emits the links after the importmap tag, so test_importmap_script_precedes_modulepreload_links passes. The developers instead chose a closed opt-in allowlist (add_import(preload: true) + get_preload_specifiers()): test_get_import_map_preloads_exactly_the_allowlisted_entries errors calling import_map::get_preload_specifiers(), which the agent did not create (an M-type name mismatch), and test_plugin_registered_import_is_not_preloaded fails because the agent preloads a hook-registered 'theme-switcher' entry, which is the design decision the issue never states. Whether plugin-registered imports should be preloaded is a genuine second reasonable reading, hence A rather than W.

The issue explicitly allows two resolutions: 'either reject Run ASAP while the task is running or preserve the request for a subsequent execution'. The agent chose preservation: it records nextruntime in scheduled_task_starting() and, in scheduled_task_complete(), keeps a nextruntime that was moved into the past while running instead of recomputing it, which satisfies the stated expectation (no silent discard). The developers chose rejection: set_scheduled_task_nextruntime() now returns bool and returns false when the cron lock is held or timestarted is set; the hidden test test_set_scheduled_task_nextruntime_rejects_running_task asserts assertFalse(...) in both cases and the existing test now does assertTrue(set_scheduled_task_nextruntime(...)), which fails against the agent's void method. Minor caveat: the agent's preservation is dropped on scheduled_task_failed(), but that path already reschedules the task soon.
